about: The owner's required questions for every design, build, recommendation and board/Gro/GAI design review (owner_approval_gates_2026-10-17.md, owner 2026-10-17: 'capture the most relevant and critical ones'). One source: bgg_call.py appends them to design prompts, bgg_prompt_bias_gate.py requires them in board prompts, record_design.py and owner_approval_capture.py require a design record to answer every one. RQ-4 (owner 2026-10-18, RULES-1018): Q40 outcome check, Q41-Q44 expert depth.

questions.q: Does this move data collection, edge evaluation or the $2.5K -> $25K goal on this PAPER account? If it is conservative, does it justify itself against growth rather than capital preservation?
questions.source: CLAUDE.md 'THIS IS A PAPER TRADING ACCOUNT'; 'NORTH-STAR-FIRST BOARD MANDATE'

questions.q: Does it change the number of trades the bot takes? More trades with conviction, never fewer: any reduction must be justified and approved by the owner.
Should this exist at all, and is there a simpler way? If a capability looks risky, what must be built to make it safe (get to yes), rather than restricting it?

What existing work already covers this: design records, the Confluence 2.0 admission registry, open or merged PRs, parallel Codex/cloud sessions, the backlog? Does it duplicate or conflict with any of it?
Is it static? Can every threshold, multiplier or number be derived from rolling or observed data instead?
questions.source: memory feedback_no_static_regimes ('Is it static?' gate); CLAUDE.md 'NO STATIC-THRESHOLD EXEMPTIONS'

questions.q: What static assumption does this expose, and what dynamic, adaptive or regime-aware capability should be built next (the forward pass)?
questions.source: CLAUDE.md 'BUILD, DON'T JUST FIX' rule A (MODE-2 forward pass)

questions.q: Is it siloed? Which other paths (scoring, sizing, entry gates, exits, scanner, risk) could it fine-tune, confirm or filter, and does each connection add signal, fail safe and stay testable?
Is every causal or performance claim backed by a measurement, a log line or a trace gathered first (else labelled a hypothesis)? Is the problem real and current in the logs?
Front-loaded simulation: which historical cases and regimes was it tested on, what effect is expected (direction and size), and what live result would prove it wrong?
questions.source: CLAUDE.md 'BUILD, DON'T JUST FIX' rules B and C

questions.q: Is a validated edge being held back only by calibration perfectionism (Profitable > Perfect)?
Does it change position size, trade frequency or concurrency/exposure, including through a multiplier upstream of the Kelly or gross caps? If so it is risk-path: board plus the masked-loss seat.
Does it touch the safety envelope: a stop on every position, the 7% daily kill switch, never-mask-a-loss, paper=True, the data-source tiers? Bounded risk is fine; widening the envelope is not.
questions.source: CLAUDE.md rule E carve-out; memory feedback_safety_control_never_mask_loss

questions.q: What happens when its data or a dependency is missing, stale or wrong? Does it fail safe?
questions.source: CLAUDE.md 'FEATURE DESIGN PROTOCOL' (failure mode); ANTI-SILO 'FAILS SAFE'

questions.q: Is any part a shadow: log-only, 'observe for N weeks', computed but not acted on? (Not allowed before $25K: ship live after the replay and the gate, or remove it.)
questions.source: CLAUDE.md 'No shadow logs or shadow periods'

questions.q: Is every decision it makes logged with its full decision stack so it can be reverse-engineered from the logs?
After it ships, what log line proves it ran, and how will it be audited and replayed against its first full trading session?
How will it be proven to work at runtime in its real process, not just present in the code?
Is an anomaly being explained away as 'by design' without re-examining the design against what actually happened?
Does it change entry, exit, sizing or strategy routing? Then the owner approves the exact design before any commit.

Self-QA: are the review prompts neutral (no leading language)? Is this a lazy take or an overclaim? Have the logs been fully reviewed? Has the design been thought ahead and taken to the board, Gro and GAI?
Can any test or check of this reach the real broker? Every new broker call must be mocked in tests, and the broker must refuse under test.
For a new fail-closed control: has it been run read-only on the server against the real broker and ledger before being called live?
questions.source: memory feedback_probe_new_controls_on_prod (2026-09-29 allocator denied all entries)

questions.q: Has a full-path simulation passed before calling it ready? Deployed is not ready.
Is any 'X doesn't exist / isn't tradable / has no ETF' claim checked against the source in this turn?
Are stock or market statistics (volatility, typical moves, behaviour) measured from data (e.g. a year of Alpaca bars), not quoted from memory?
Data source: which tier (T1 Alpaca / T2 FMP / T3 breadth CSV / T4 yfinance only for VIX, VIX3M, JPY), which API, and what is the fallback behaviour?
Output: where does it write, in what format, and is an atomic write required?
Integration point: where in the existing flow does this connect, and what runs before and after it (threading, the run_cycle thread, check_exits)?
questions.source: CLAUDE.md 'FEATURE DESIGN PROTOCOL' item 3; 'COLD SECOND-AGENT REVIEW' runtime context

questions.q: Value rank: where does this rank against the other open items by expected value toward $25K per session of work, and why is it next?
questions.source: handoff.md Alignment Gate ('## Value rank'); MODE-2 'ITERATION PATH' (Master Brain 2026-10-17)

questions.q: Whitespace and blind spots: what does a standard quantitative execution framework require here that the bot lacks, and what risk would our own audit (10-point, RC classes, board) underweight?
questions.source: CLAUDE.md 'NORTH STAR PERSONA MANDATE' MODE 2 (Master Brain 2026-10-17)

questions.q: Out of sample: was it tested walk-forward or with purged cross-validation, how many variants were tried, and is the result still significant after that many tries (deflated Sharpe)? (The answer informs size and the reversal criterion; it never justifies a shadow or 'wait for N trades' period before $25K.)
questions.source: hedge-fund beta-model review (owner 2026-10-17); Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning

questions.q: Data honesty: could the replay contain look-ahead (using a bar before it closed), survivorship (only today's symbols), or data snooping?
Costs: are spread, slippage, missed fills and partial fills in the replay, and what do live fills show the real cost to be?
questions.source: hedge-fund beta-model review (owner 2026-10-17); CLAUDE.md roadmap TCA item

questions.q: Alpha or beta: how much of the expected return is just exposure to SPY, a sector or momentum, and what is left after removing it?
questions.source: hedge-fund beta-model review (owner 2026-10-17); Asness / AQR factor research

questions.q: Regimes and tails: how does it behave in high-VIX, trending and choppy markets, what is its worst day, and how correlated is it with what the book already holds?
Capacity and liquidity: does it still work at the $25K account size and in thin names (share of average daily volume, IEX-only quotes)?

Statistical power: how many trades are needed to tell this edge from noise, how many exist now, and what is the confidence interval on its expected value per trade? (The answer informs size and the reversal criterion; it never justifies a shadow or 'wait for N trades' period before $25K.)
Decay and replacement: how is edge decay measured, and what owner-approved definition of 'non-working' moves it to zero trades and triggers its replacement?
questions.source: owner 2026-10-17 (strategies are never paused automatically; a non-working strategy takes zero trades and is replaced)

questions.q: Sizing follows edge: is the size tied to the measured win rate and payoff (Kelly fraction) rather than a fixed number, and is the P&L that feeds it taken from Alpaca fills?
questions.source: hedge-fund beta-model review (owner 2026-10-17); memory feedback_pnl_sourcing; project_kelly_config

questions.q: Outcome owned: which result does this protect, and what machine-evaluated check proves the result holds (a result check, not 'the code/block is present'; or 'none' with the reason)?
questions.source: article 'How to be more ambitious' (Felix Rieseberg) rules, owner approval RULES-1018 2026-10-18

questions.q: What would the best expert in this field do beyond what was asked?
questions.source: article 'How to be more ambitious' (Felix Rieseberg) rules, owner approval RULES-1018 2026-10-18

questions.q: What is the rawest data available for this (broker fills, bars, logged decision stacks), and is that what it uses rather than a summary?
questions.source: article 'How to be more ambitious' (Felix Rieseberg) rules, owner approval RULES-1018 2026-10-18

questions.q: What is the professional method for this problem, and does the design use it?
questions.source: article 'How to be more ambitious' (Felix Rieseberg) rules, owner approval RULES-1018 2026-10-18

questions.q: What independent evidence (not the author grading its own work) will prove it works?
questions.source: article 'How to be more ambitious' (Felix Rieseberg) rules, owner approval RULES-1018 2026-10-18
